newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 240 bln levs March 1.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 240 bln levs March 1.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 18 billion levs in the first half of March to 240 billion levs, preliminary Finance Ministry figures showed.
The rise in the deficit was due to payments on Bulgaria's huge domestic debt, a Finance ministry official said.
Further details were not immediately available.

Bulgaria's domestic debt rose to 2,778 billion levs at end-February from 1,053 billion levs a month earlier due to the sharp lev fall against the dollar and new government securities issued to finance public spending.

The deficit at mid-March was around 1.2 percent of the nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for this year assumed in the memorandum of economic policies agreed by the government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) last week.
The budget deficit for the whole of 1997 was set at 3.8 percent of projected nominal GDP set at 20.743 trillion levs, down a real 4.8 percent from 1996.

Figures for spending, revenue and deficit as percentage of targets are not available because a viable budget for 1997 has yet to be passed by the new parliament due to assemble after elections in April.
Under a stop-gap budget bill approved on January 31 the deficit was limited to the amount of interest payments due on government debt.

Last week the interim government, in office until after April 19 election committed itself to strict financial discipline to prepare the implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime by the new government in June.
Under an agreement with the IMF pending an approval by the IMF board in the second week of April Bulgaria is to be supported through a $510 million stand-by facility.
To balance its budget without central bank financing Bulgaria is to set up a fiscal reserve account under the agreement.

The account would be set up on the basis of the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development (SFRD) and would include current budget and extra-budgetary deposits, privatisation proceeds and external financing, the finance ministry official said.
The SFRD which contains proceeds from sell-offs and external loans now has some $65 million. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
